persons.name: Levi F. Arnold
persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'E F, Arnold, P.M.' and 'L. F. ARNOLD, P. ?.' and 'L. F. ARNOLD, P.M.' and 'LEVI F. ARNOLD, P.M.' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 28; the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 39; the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 14; the Democrat of 21 January 1835, column 7. The corpus associates the name with Plainfield; that is where the paper does business with this person and not a statement about where they slept, and the storefront tickets are the ones that may stand a shop there. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `postmaster` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'A. Gartetl's Auctiog Rowe' and 'A. Gatren' and 'GARRETT,' and 'RRSTT' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the American of 25 July 1835, column 3; the American of 15 August 1835, column 2; the Democrat of 17 December 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 24 December 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 12 August 1835, column 5. The corpus associates the name with Dearborn Street, South Water Street; that is where the paper does business with this person and not a statement about where they slept, and the storefront tickets are the ones that may stand a shop there. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `auctioneer` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 5 times, as “GARRETT A”, “GARRETT AUGUST”, 1836-06-21 to 1836-06-23: 5 lots in the platted town — lot 5 of block 41 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L5BL41CHIOT, as printed); lot 7 of block 31 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L7BL31CHIOT, as printed); lot 8 of block 53 in the town the register codes CHIOTV (L8B53CHIOTV, as printed); the N2 of lot 8 of block 53 in the town the register codes CHIOT (N2L8B53CHIOT, as printed); the N2S2 of lot 8 of block 53 in the town the register codes CHI (N2S2L8B53CHI, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $15960.00 (ls1162, ls1163, ls1164, ls1165, ls1166). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $15960.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: GARRETT A matches A. Garrett: the forename names A. Garrett of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

persons.name: Henry J Ostrum
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented once and corroborated by nothing else, so the weakest rung of `inferred` the owner's ladder defines. A SINGLE APPEARANCE AND NOTHING ELSE. Read from poll_1834. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G3), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1834 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Ostrum, Henry J.” (poll_1834_083, line 252). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Ostrum' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Powers, T.W, >' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 22 October 1834, column 3 — dated 1834-10-22. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
